source.title: Aligned Training: A Parameter-Free Method to Improve Feature Quality and Stability of Sparse Autoencoders (SAE)

record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-seed feature-dictionary stability and finds standard SAEs unstable, while aligned training improves stability. This refines the claim that SAE features are stable canonical units; it does not test the original toy-model superposition result.
record.gate_note: The cross-seed stability results in Figure 6 bear on V5. The paper's reconstruction, dead-feature, spurious-correlation, alignment-score, MCS, and autointerpretability results do not test the versions' named behaviors and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper proposing aligned training for SAEs. Its stability result (Fig. 6) compares the authors' own reparameterization against standard training. It reports no readable stability values for standard SAEs. Its statement that standard SAEs are substantially unstable is cited from prior work [25, 32], not measured here. No result bears on whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units, so V5 is not tested. V1–V4 and V6 are not addressed.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that aligned training, a parameter-free constraint fixing each feature's encoder–decoder inner product to 1, gives Pareto reconstruction gains, near-zero dead features and more stable dictionaries across seeds. They attribute the stability gain to removing a rotational degree of freedom. They claim these gains hold across models, sizes and architectures, but stability itself is shown only for Gemma 2 2B, layer 12, 65K.
record.recipe_differences: This study evaluates an SAE reparameterization and its effects on feature quality and stability; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported stability comparison is for ReLU and TopK SAEs at Gemma 2 2B layer 12, dictionary size 65K; the text reports improvement for both architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-seed decoder agreement (MMCS) is higher under aligned training than standard training for ReLU and TopK SAEs (Gemma 2 2B, layer 12, 65K), with the gap opening early in training (Fig. 6). The figure gives no numbers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-seed agreement of SAE dictionaries depends on the SAE's encoder–decoder parameterization.

fits_no_version.finding: Encoder–decoder alignment scores of pretrained SAEs are bimodal (Pythia 70M, LLaMA 3 8B IT, Gemma 2 2B). The scores correlate with MCS (r=0.65) and autointerpretability (r=0.32). The authors conjecture that near-zero-alignment features are training artifacts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A substantial fraction of standard SAE features are low-quality training artifacts rather than model units.

record.problems: The stability findings are presented in a figure without exact values or stated uncertainty. The stability experiment covers one model, layer, and dictionary size, and MMCS measures cross-seed decoder-dictionary agreement rather than completeness or canonicality.
record.rows_left_out: Reconstruction and dead-feature results (Sections 4.2–4.3 and Figures 2–5, 15–20), SCR results (Section 4.6 and Figure 9), and alignment-score/MCS/autointerpretability results (Appendix C, Figures 10–12) were left out because they do not measure the behaviors named by the tested version.

untested.parts: Toy-model superposition geometry and sparsity transition. The paper's 2-D toy model concerns SAE encoder–decoder alignment, not superposition.
Whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or recoverable by SAEs. SAEs are used as a tool only.
Completeness, stability and canonicality of SAE features. No readable standard-SAE stability numbers are given, and the instability claim is cited from prior work.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 'challenges' label rested on cited prior work (Paulo & Belrose; Song et al.), not on this study's measurements, so it is dropped. The 'limits_scope' label rested on an own-method comparison, so it is dropped too. Stability results are figure-only, with no uncertainty and no stated number of seeds.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, feature sparsity, overlap geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features are spread across neurons or sparse features can be recovered by a dictionary.

Only cross-seed stability of SAE decoder dictionaries is measured, for Gemma 2 2B at layer 12 and dictionary size 65K. Completeness and canonicality are not tested; other models and dictionary sizes are not tested for stability.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared cross-seed mean min cosine similarity (MMCS) of decoder dictionaries for standard and aligned ReLU SAEs during training.

conditions.value: throughout training; figure plots up to 70,000 steps

rows.measure: MMCS between decoder dictionaries of independently trained SAEs; higher scores indicate greater agreement.
rows.value: figure only: aligned training; the text says aligned training improves cross-seed stability.
rows.note: The authors say aligned training achieves consistently lower cosine distance and that the gap opens early. No exact MMCS values are stated in the text.
rows.check: The row compares the study's own method (aligned) with a standard ReLU baseline, so it is a method-performance comparison, not a test of V5. Values are figure-only and no MMCS numbers are stated. Standard-SAE instability is asserted by citing [25, 32], not measured as a result here.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared cross-seed mean min cosine similarity (MMCS) of decoder dictionaries for standard and aligned TopK SAEs during training.

conditions.value: throughout training; figure plots up to 140,000 steps

rows.measure: MMCS between decoder dictionaries of independently trained SAEs; higher scores indicate greater agreement.
rows.value: figure only: aligned training; the text says aligned training improves cross-seed stability.
rows.note: The authors say aligned training achieves consistently lower cosine distance and that the gap opens early. No exact MMCS values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Same issue for TopK (k=20): this is an own-method vs. baseline comparison with figure-only values. The text mislabels the axis as 'lower cosine distance' while the plot shows a stability score (MMCS).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: The study describes standard SAEs as substantially unstable across seeds, challenging the claim that SAE features are generally stable canonical units (R1, R2).
